title: Lionfish USB Keypad Interceptor Architecture & Device Detection Milestone
content:
Lionfish reached its first major milestone as a native Windows desktop application dedicated to hardware-level USB keypad interception and macro automation. Built within the JeffersonWM monorepo (apps/lionfish), the project isolates secondary input devices—specifically a 34-key mechanical numeric keypad and an 8-button programmable macro pad with rotary knob—so that their keystrokes trigger macros, application launches, and browser shortcuts without interfering with standard typing on the primary keyboard.

What changed:

  • Core Interception & Driver Architecture: Built on .NET 10 with WPF and the CommunityToolkit.Mvvm pattern, integrated with the low-level Interception kernel driver (InputInterceptorNS) for true OS-level keystroke blocking. First-run setup automatically detects driver state and handles administrative UAC elevation.
  • Safety Guard & Master Protection: Built a hardware failsafe with an emergency kill switch triggered by pressing Left Ctrl + Right Ctrl simultaneously. The built-in laptop keyboard (ACPI/PS2 bus HPQ8001) is automatically recognized and protected as the Master Keyboard so it can never be locked out.
  • Interactive 'Press to Identify' Mode: Wired a Windows Raw Input sink (WM_INPUT with RIDEV_INPUTSINK) into the window. Clicking 'Identify Device' or pressing any button on any keypad instantly pinpoints the physical hardware device, highlights it orange in the list, displays the exact key pressed, and offers one-click role assignment.
  • Hardware Classification: Differentiates built-in laptop keyboards, external USB macro pads (VID_258E&PID_000F), and 2.4GHz wireless keyboards (VID_045E&PID_07B2), while filtering out virtual software drivers.
  • Smart App Control (0x800711C7) Resolution: Resolved Windows 11 Smart App Control policy blocks by consolidating the Core interception engine directly into the application project, compiling everything into a unified Lionfish.exe binary with zero loose DLL dependencies.
  • Process Launcher & System Tray: Created apps/lionfish/run.ps1 with single-instance detection, system tray background notices, and interactive restart prompts. The app minimizes cleanly to the Windows system tray with left-click toggle and right-click profile switching.

This milestone establishes the foundational hardware abstraction and interception layer for Lionfish. With reliable device identification, driver-level blocking, and failsafe safety guards in place, the path is clear for building out custom key mappings, macro recording, and site-specific browser automation.
